It gives an evaluation of H nonzero with every coordinate nonzero; m>=1 makes that vector nonzero. This is stronger than the stated homogeneous case; no homogeneity hypothesis is needed.

title: A nonzero homogeneous form over an infinite field has a nonvanishing direction
statement: Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], let $m\ge 1$, and let $H$ be a nonzero homogeneous polynomial in $k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. There exists a nonzero vector $v\in k^m$ with $H(v)\ne0$ (equivalently, the one-dimensional subspace $kv$ is not contained in the zero locus of $H$).

source.place: §3.2.4, the Noether-normalization direction choice (expanded elementary polynomial argument)
